newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse consolidates its upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse consolidates its upward trend.

text.p: Moroccan stock market ended the week on Friday higher pulled up by main largest capitalisation stocks, especially the second largest holding Societe Nationale d'Investissement, stockbrokers said.
The bourse share index closed at an all-time high to 402.56 points, up from 399.88 points last week.
With a capitalisation of more than 5.5 billion dirhams, SNI rose 15 points to close at 575 dirhams. The conglomerate has a diversified interests in more than 40 Moroccan companies.
ONA Group, the country's largest private group, closed at 410 dirhams, up from 405 a week earlier.
Wafabank, one of market blue chips, rose 12 dirhams to at 432 dirhams.
Credit Eqdom, the largest consumer credit company surged by 26 dirhams to close at 866 dirhams.
"The company gained 8.25 percent since the beginning of the year due to its leading position in Moroccan credit sector," Mohemd Mekouar, a prominent analyst at Upline Securities told Reuters.
The company just announced 17 dirhams dividend payment for the 1995 fiscal year. The state floated 200,000 shares, or 18 percent stake of EQDOM on the Casablanca stock market in 1995.
"It recorded the best earning per share growth from 46 million dirhams in 1994 to 114 million dirhams in 1995, which pushed the closing price from 400 dirhams to 800 dirhams," Mekouar said.
Upline Securities stockbrokers forecast a conservative 91 million dirhams net income in 1996, he said.

Upline Securities Index (USI.CS, which tracks the 10 most liquid stocks, closed at 51,936 points, up from 51,104 points last Friday "recording an all-time year to day preformance 23.87 percent," he added.
The bourse total volume rose slightly to 17.08 million dirhams from 16.2 million dirhams in last Friday's session.
